best_for: Players and ROM hackers who want an accurate Game Boy Advance emulator that also runs Game Boy and Game Boy Color games, with no BIOS file to hunt down.
description:
mGBA is a Game Boy Advance emulator written mostly by one developer, Jeffrey Pfau, who made its first commit in 2013. The project says it runs at full speed even on low-end machines such as netbooks.

Hold Tab to fast-forward through slow parts and the backquote key to rewind a mistake. You get 9 save state slots, each shown with a screenshot, and you can record play as video, GIF, WebP or APNG. Games load straight from ZIP and 7z files, and IPS, UPS and BPS patches apply fan translations and ROM hacks. The e-Reader is supported too. For debugging, it offers a command line and a GDB remote link that works with Ghidra and IDA Pro, and it is also available as a core for RetroArch and OpenEmu.

points.title: Three handhelds in one
points.text: mGBA runs Game Boy Advance games and also Game Boy and Game Boy Color, so one app covers the whole Nintendo handheld line before the DS.

points.title: No BIOS needed
points.text: It ships its own BIOS replacement, so games start without a dump from real hardware. You can still load an original BIOS file if you have one.

points.title: Odd hardware is covered
points.text: It handles the real-time clock without setup, the Boktai solar sensor, the Game Boy Camera and Printer, and motion and rumble when you use a controller. Save types are detected automatically, though flash size detection misses in some games.

points.title: Link play stays on one machine
points.text: Link cable emulation works only between windows on the same computer. Playing over a network is still listed as a planned feature.

points.title: Cheats and Lua scripting
points.text: Cheat codes are supported, and GameShark and Action Replay snapshots can be loaded and exported. Lua scripting gives scripts access to memory, save states and input.

points.title: Stable release is from 2025
points.text: 0.10.5 came out on March 8, 2025. Newer fixes land in development builds first. mGBA is open source under the Mozilla Public License 2.0.

points.title: Platform notes
points.text: Windows installers come in 32-bit and 64-bit and install for all users; that listing keeps 19 versions. The Mac app is universal, and the project also offers a legacy build for macOS 10.9. The Linux Flatpak is a Flathub build not marked as verified; the project itself ships AppImages.
